what: 20-yr average illumination at published validation points, our model vs literature
window: 2026-01-01 .. 2046-01-01, 6 h steps (Sun from JPL DE421 via skyfield)
model: 360-azimuth horizon from LOLA LDEM_75S_240M (240 m/px, bilinear), rays to 150 km; Sun as a disc (0.27 deg radius) for disc-average %, centre for 'centre' %. Mast 0 m = surface; 2 m = 2 m above ground. compare_pct uses surface for surface rows and 2 m for the 2 m row.

results.name: Connecting Ridge C1
results.source: Mazarico et al. 2011 Icarus 211:1066 (via Gläser 2018 Table 1)

results.name: Connecting Ridge C1 (Gläser, 20 m DTM, surface)
Connecting Ridge C1, 2 m above ground
Shackleton rim S
results.source: Mazarico et al. 2011 (via Gläser 2018 Table 1); Gläser: 81.0/85.5%, 221 h shadow

gaps: Literature uses 20 m (Glaser, LOLA/LROC NAC DTM) or 240 m (Mazarico) DEMs; ours is the 240 m LOLA grid, so sharp ridge crests are smoothed and small-scale shadows are missed.

Points within a few hundred metres differ by 10+ points on ridges, so a coordinate offset of one DEM pixel matters (v2 failed the 2 m Gläser point by 26 points for this reason; v3 reads heights bilinearly and agrees within 3 points).
Earth visibility is not validated against a published table; it is pure geometry plus the same horizon mask.
The 3D view uses a 360 m/px resampled height map for shading, coarser than the 240 m masks.
Lander assumptions: we model a point observer 2 m above ground; real antenna/solar panel heights and the lander's own shadow are not modelled.
Only 4 validation points, all on the Shackleton / connecting-ridge area; the other regions and grid cells are not checked against literature.
Connecting Ridge C1 vs Mazarico 2011: we are 12 points lower at the surface (77 vs 89%); Mazarico used a different DEM and point, so the gap is not fully explained.

v2_results.note: v2 (2-yr window, 64 azimuths, nearest-pixel observer height, 2 m mast for all rows)
v2_results.cause: v2 read the observer height from the floored DEM pixel, which on a narrow ridge crest put the observer below the crest; v3 uses bilinear heights for observer and terrain
